contracts: Only validated C5 cold-ROM load selects the optional CPU PMA/PMP owner; other SoCs keep existing CSR storage when disabled.

Actual guest CSR instructions use checked reads and writes. CSRRW/CSRRWI rd=x0 omit old-value reads. Unsupported preserves the reason and stops the host model without writing guest exception CSRs or destinations.

CPU observer refreshes immutable policy snapshots only at epoch/generation changes before each instruction. Fetch/load/store and LR/SC/RMW are checked before device effects; complete 32-bit fetch spans are checked before the high half.

Known Deny remains an architectural access fault. Unknown POR/WARL/overlap/other unqualified cases become Fault::Unsupported -> Trap::ModelLimit(pc) -> unconditional Stop::ModelLimit, with no invented raw instruction or guest exception. The debug unimplemented-instruction switch cannot override this stop.
CLIC SHV resolves the vector read before committing guest entry state. An unknown vector preserves mepc/mcause/mtval/mstatus/mil/reservation/waiting; genuine prohibited-vector behavior retains MINHV.
CPU policy locks survive ROM byte replacement and profile deselection. Only actual core reset clears locks and advances epoch; failed reset generation arithmetic stays fail-closed.
Host inspection has no guest instruction context; DMA uses independent APM and transport boundaries. Both ordinary and priced observer early-stop paths clean the CPU context.

Plain/priced unknown Fetch/Load/Store/AMO leave guest trap state unchanged even with stop_on_unimplemented=false
